profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, tagged telecom=data_center, is named "Factory Software | AVEVA Select Italia." AVEVA is a real, publicly traded industrial software company, listed on the London Stock Exchange, that provides engineering design, operations management, and asset-performance software used across manufacturing, energy, and process industries worldwide. "AVEVA Select" is the branding AVEVA uses for its network of regional reseller and systems-integrator partners, and this record most plausibly identifies an Italian partner office selling and supporting AVEVA's software products under that program, likely operating under the name "Factory Software" as the local reseller entity. A software reseller and integrator's office maintains its own business IT systems but is not a data-center operator; the telecom=data_center tag here is best read as a mistag of the office's own server or IT closet.

reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point tagged as a data center in Italy is a software reseller's office, not a data center. The record carries zero megawatts, no operator, and no website.

The name resolves to AVEVA Select Italia, the branding AVEVA uses for regional resellers and systems integrators of its industrial software. A partner office runs its own business IT, which is likely what the tag captured. The reading itself concludes the telecom=data_center tag is a mistag of an office server closet.

For AI scaling this is a data-quality signal, not a capacity signal. Any count of Italian data centers drawn from this tag would include at least one software office, so such counts overstate the building stock that compute depends on. The record sits 1.2 miles from Milan Malpensa, which says nothing about power or interconnection.

What the data does not cover is how often this mistag occurs. One point cannot establish a rate, and no other facilities are given for comparison. It also gives no grid, power, or capacity figure for any real facility, so it cannot speak to the binding constraint at all.
